Watchfield Primary School
Welcome to Watchfield! We are a busy, but very friendly school with lots going on. This website aims to give you a taste of the school, as well as providing regular updated information for both parents and pupils. However, the only way you can really get a sense of what it is like to be 'a Watchfielder', is to come and visit.
An education here is a truly unique experience. Watchfield is a diverse school; many of our children come from countries all over the world, yet we still maintain the supportive family ethos of a village school, with strong links to the local community.
Our Pre-School
Watchfield Primary School Pre-school has been rated Good by Ofsted and is proud to be part of the Cambrian Learning Trust family of Schools. We are a team of experienced, dedicated and passionate Early Years Educators. Our aim is for our children to have a happy and fulfilled time in our Pre-school, following the Prime Areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage so that their transition into Reception School Year is seamless. We will support your child to develop the skills required to enable them to build a solid foundation at this crucial first steppingstone in their educational journey.

Governors
A warm welcome to you from your school governors! The Local Governing Committee (LGC) plays an important part in the life of your school. The members of the LGC reflect a wide range of interests from local businesses and the community, staff members and, of course, parents. Our LGC is composed of Trust-appointed Governors, elected Parent and Staff Governors, the Head of School and Executive Head (by virtue of the office they hold).
As we are part of a Multi-Academy Trust, the Watchfield Primary School LGC is accountable to the Cambrian Learning Trust Board. The Board assigns local governance responsibilities to the LGC, in accordance with the Scheme of Delegated Authority and LGC Terms of Reference. The LGC provides oversight of the school's management, performance and finances, in line with the development plan for the Trust. The LGC also ensures Trust-wide and local policies are implemented and monitored, and that meeting and reporting structures are aligned with those of the Board.
The LGC recognise and understand that our school is unique. We take a keen interest in school performance data but recognise the data is but one measure of a child's performance. One of our strengths is in the whole school experience at Watchfield where a child's mind, body and spirit benefits from the rich tapestry of cultures, nationalities and experiences that the children in our school bring. Consequently, the LGC has an important job to do in ensuring that the welfare of the school and its culture, values and ethos are maintained.
The role of governors is one of both challenge and support in a constructive way. We are always open to feedback and ideas. If you would like to offer a suggestion, your governors can be contacted by email to the clerk to the LGC : Mr Shaf Moledina SMoledina@cambrianlt.org
Minutes, agendas and reports of all LGC Meetings are available for inspection in school, by arrangement upon request, from the Clerk to Governors (SMoledina@cambrianlt.org)

Meet the Governors
DIANA SHELDON (Chair) (Safeguarding), Trust Governor
Appointed: July 2024 Term: 4 years
First Appointed : July 2020
My first connection with the school was when my eldest attended in year 2 during a short posting to Watchfield in 1986! Obviously, many things have changed over the years including the arrival of the Defence Academy. Since settling back in Shrivenham in 2011 I have known many children, parents and members of staff at the school. I am conscious of what a wonderful job is done in such a unique environment and everyone I know enjoys their time at Watchfield as well as having a great educational experience.
"Having been a teacher for almost 40 years, in many different schools, I am well aware of the challenges and pressures that face the staff and governors. I am honoured to have been selected as a governor to have the chance to support all the hard work that goes on at Watchfield school in order that every child has the opportunity to reach their full potential in the time they are there."
AARON DEACON (Vice-Chair) (SEND), Parent Governor
Appointed: Mar 2024 Term: 4 years
I live locally and have been part of the community for six years. I have two children currently attending the school, with a third due to join soon, which gives me a strong personal connection and understanding of the school environment. I’ve been a governor at the school for around nine months and currently serve as Vice Chair as well as the Link Governor for Inclusion and SEND. I’m particularly passionate about continual improvement, helping the school evolve and perform at its best for every pupil. I wanted to use my knowledge, skills, and experience to support the school and its leadership team. Having close family members who have served as headteachers and executive heads, I’ve always appreciated the vital role schools play at the heart of a community. Being a governor allows me to contribute to that work and help ensure the best possible outcomes for every child.
I work as Head of DevOps and Platform Engineering at Prolinx, where I lead teams focused on designing and delivering secure, scalable IT platforms. Outside of work and school commitments, I’m a keen Arsenal supporter and enjoy getting to games whenever I can. I also like relaxing with gaming and spending time with family - though I’ll admit I often find my-self working on one project or another.
YVONNE ANDREWS, Trust Appointed Governor
Appointed: March 2024 Term: 4 years
I previously taught at Watchfield Primary School for many years, leaving my role as Blackbird’s teacher in December 2021 to join the Defence Cyber Academy as a cyber instructor. I was able to bring my teaching experience to the academy whilst learning the relevant cyber knowledge. In 2022, I became the leader of the cyber instructor team and responsible for ensuring the curriculum is delivered correctly. Although I no longer work in the Primary sector, I have retained a keen interest in the education of young children, and particularly the great work of Watchfield Primary School. Therefore, I was delighted to take up the role of community governor of WPS
DANNI WILLIAMS, Parent Governor
Appointed: May 2025 Term: 4 years
I have two girls at Watchfield in Years 1 and 5. I wanted to be more involved in our children's education and help out where I can. I have worked in financial services for 15+ years looking after global accounts and partnerships. I'm currently working for a large fintech looking after their cross-border product for the UK. A lot of what I do in my job is strategic and I hope I can be of some use to make Watchfield as amazing as possible. I am new to the governor role and look after health and safety and the overall curriculum. As a family, we love to travel. We have explored the far east and have recently started skiing lessons in preparation for the winter season. We also spend a lot of time outdoors on our bikes or walking in our wellies.
JOANNA RYAN, Staff Governor
Appointed: June 2022 Term: 4 years
Upon qualifying as a teacher in 2015, Jo took up her first position at Watchfield and she has never looked back. Jo has spent the subsequent seven years teaching across KS2 and has just returned from maternity leave. She is passionate about reading (both in and out of school!) and is currently enjoying being back at work as well as spending time with her new family.
"I care deeply about this school and the families that we are privileged to meet and teach here. I am excited to have the opportunity to work with the other governors to support the school over the coming years."
CLARE HARTLEY, Staff Governor
Appointed: Sep 2022 Term: 4 years
I have been a teacher for a number of years, working in schools in the UK and further afield. I have taught at Watchfield since 2014, with two years out teaching in the Middle East. Outside school, I enjoy reading and gardening. I run the choir at St. Andrew's church in Shrivenham and am passionate about choral music.
JOHN BOWEN, Trust Appointed Governor
Appointed: May 2025 Term: 4 years
My son attends Watchfield Primary school and is having an excellent time in the duckling's class. I considered becoming a governor because I recently spent two years teaching at the Defence Academy and caught the educational bug. Supporting my local community and heling shape the educational environment for my, and all, children is important to me. I work for the British Army and my hobbies and interests include rugby, cricket, boxing, mountain sports, dog walking and reading.
JUDE SCUTT (Executive Head)
Appointed: Sep 2022 Term: Ongoing
Within my role of Executive Headteacher, I have the opportunity to support the school from a strategic and operational position. I have 15 years’ experience of leadership in a range of context so I can bring a variety of skills and knowledge to support our school to be the best it can be.
NICK HATCLIFFE (Head of School)
Appointed: Sep 2025 Term: Ongoing
I'm Nick Hatcliffe, and I'm excited to lead the wonderful team at Watchfield Primary School. I'm passionate about teaching, learning and making the most of outdoor education to inspire and engage children. I'm committed to driving continuous school improvement by building on our strengths, developing high-quality teaching, and ensuring every child has the opportunity to thrive. With over six years of experience as a school governor, I currently serve on the governing boards of two local primary schools, where I enjoy supporting leadership teams, sharing best practice, and working collaboratively to raise standards across our communities. I'm proud to work alongside our dedicated staff, families, and the wider community to continue developing our vibrant, inclusive and forward-thinking school.
CARRIE INSLEY, Parent Governor
Appointed Mar 2026 Term Ongoing:
As a military mum, my children have attended Watchfield Primary several times. Now that we are permanent residents in the village, I am delighted to have been appointed as a governor so that I can give something back to this incredible community. As a logistics and personnel officer in the Royal Navy, I bring a variety of skills to the role, in particular my experience in leadership, assurance and creating effective organisations. I am looking forward to helping Watchfield Primary continue to thrive and deliver the best possible outcomes for every child.
SHAF MOLEDINA (Clerk to Governors)

Young Carers
At Watchfield we are aware that some of our pupils are young carers. A young carer is someone under 18 who is caring unpaid for a family member, sibling or friend who is ill, frail, disabled or has mental health or addiction problems. They often take on a practical and/or emotional caring responsibilities that would normally be expected of an adult.
We know that young carers may need a little extra support to enjoy and do well at school. At Watchfield we are committed to ensuring that all pupils who are young carers are identified and supported effectively.
If you feel your child may be a Young Carer, please contact the school office.

Cambrian Learning Trust is committed to supporting young carers to access education.
This policy aims to ensure young carers in all our schools are identified and offered appropriate support to access the education to which they are entitled.
A young carer is a child or young person who is helping to look after someone at home. Most are caring for a parent, commonly in a single parent family, but some may be taking responsibility for a sibling, grandparent or other relative.

pageCache.pageTitle: Watchfield Primary School - English as an additional language (EAL)
pageCache.text:
English as an additional language (EAL)
Due to the proximity to the Defence Academy, Watchfield is a very diverse school. Many of our international pupils arrive in September speaking little or no English.
When a pupils arrives, we assess their English proficiency using an online platform that aligns with the DfE proficiency scale and guidance from The Bell Foundation. If the assessment shows that a child meets criteria, we are able to offer bespoke English Lessons using 'Racing to English' as a starting point for our curriculum.
English proficiency
A: New to English: May use first language for learning and other purposes. May remain completely silent in the classroom. May be copying/repeating some words or phrases. May understand some everyday expressions in English but may have minimal or no literacy in English. Needs a considerable amount of EAL support.
B: Early acquisition: May follow day-to-day social communication in English and participate in learning activities with support. Beginning to use spoken English for social purposes. May understand simple instructions and can follow narrative/accounts with visual support. May have developed some skills in reading and writing. May have become familiar with some subject specific vocabulary. Still needs a significant amount of EAL support to access the curriculum.
C: Developing competence: May participate in learning activities with increasing independence. Able to express self orally in English, but structural inaccuracies are still apparent. Literacy will require ongoing support, particularly for understanding text and writing. May be able to follow abstract concepts and more complex written English. Requires ongoing EAL support to access the curriculum fully.
D: Competent: Oral English will be developing well, enabling successful engagement in activities across the curriculum. Can read and understand a wide variety of texts. Written English may lack complexity and contain occasional evidence of errors in structure. Needs some support to access subtle nuances of meaning, to refine English usage, and to develop abstract vocabulary. Needs some/occasional EAL support to access complex curriculum material and tasks.
E: Fluent: Can operate across the curriculum to a level of competence equivalent to that of a pupil who uses English as his/her first language. Operates without EAL support across the curriculum.
We continue to offer bespoke English language lessons to pupils with EAL who need it throughout the year: children return to main class English lessons when they have developed sufficient English vocabulary to be able to access the learning.
Our EAL learners make enormous progress at our school: frequently they begin the year not speaking any English beyond ‘hello’ and they leave us speaking English fluently.

Watchfield Primary Pre-School
Watchfield Primary School Pre-school is proud to be part of the Cambrian Learning Trust family of Schools. We call ourselves the “Ducklings” who are led by a team of experienced, dedicated and passionate Early Years Educators.
Our aim is for our children to have a happy and fulfilled time in our Pre-school, following the Prime Areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage so that their transition into Reception School Year is seamless. We will support your child to develop the skills required to enable them to build a solid foundation at this crucial first steppingstone in their educational journey.
Our Pre-School is well equipped both inside and outside and we pride ourselves on the quality of provision that available. Our outside provision space is newly developed to a high specification and designed to meet the children’s developmental needs. We value the close relationships we form with the whole family and welcome opportunities to chat about your child’s development, either face to face or via our School App system.
Our Ducklings benefit from regular on-site Forest Schools sessions and integration at whole school events within the Primary School Setting. These may include watching school performances, Sports Day, Arts Week, International Week and many transition events.
For further information please contact: office@wat.cambrianlt.org

pageCache.pageTitle: Watchfield Primary School - School trips and residential visit
pageCache.text:
School trips and residential visit
School trips
We know the benefits of school trips - of children getting away from our school site and learning in a different environment. We aim to take children from all year groups on at least one trip each school year. Please see individual class pages for more details.
Residential Visit
Each year pupils in Years 5 & 6 are given the opportunity to participate in a residential visit. We believe this is an invaluable growing up experience for them, and it is always thoroughly enjoyed. There is a charge for these visits, with payments spread out over the beginning of the academic year. If you would like to discuss options regarding a bespoke payment plan, then please ask to speak to the Headteacher.
The children who do not go on the residential spend time in school participating in a range of fun activities.

SEND
Welcome to the Special Educational Needs and/or Disability (SEND) section of the Watchfield School website.
Watchfield is a welcoming and caring school where dedicated practitioners are committed to meeting our children’s needs.
The Watchfield School community is proud to be fully inclusive and celebrate diversity in all of its forms.
Below are links to documents and information that we hope you will find useful in understanding how we support our children that have special educational needs and/or disabilities.
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch.
SENDCo: Miss J Titterington
senco@wat.cambrianlt.org
SEND Governor: Aaron Deacon
What is our SEND Policy?
As part of the Cambrian Learning Trust, our policy for SEND is consistent with all the schools in the Trust.
How do we identify and support a child with SEND at our school?
This document outlines how we go about identifying, supporting and meeting the needs of pupils with SEND at Watchfield Primary School. We hope it answers questions you may have.
How do we make sure the school is accessible to all learners?
This plan shows how Watchfield intends, over time, to increase the accessibility of our school for disabled pupils, staff, parents/carers and visitors.
If you'd like to read our SEND Accessibility Plan, please visit our Policies page.
